'''''Linum catharticum''''', also known as '''purging flax''',<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.sssi.naturalengland.org.uk/citation/citation_photo/1003854.pdf |title=Lardon Chase |publisher=Natural England |accessdate=2 February 2016 |url-status=dead |archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20160202155758/http://www.sssi.naturalengland.org.uk/citation/citation_photo/1003854.pdf |archivedate= 2 February 2016 }}</ref> or '''fairy flax''', is an herbaceous flowering plant in the family [[Linaceae]], native to [[Great Britain]],<ref>{{cite web|title=Native flora recorded from postal district CO4 (Colchester area north)|url=http://www.nhm.ac.uk/fff-pcp/glob.pl?report=pcfllist&group=&sort=&inpostcode=co4|work=The Postcode Plant Database|publisher=Natural History Museum|accessdate=10 January 2013}}</ref> [[Iceland]],<ref Name="HH&GGE2004"/> central Europe and [[Western Asia]]. It is an [[annual plant]] and blooms in July and August.

It is a known host of the [[pathogen]]ic fungus [[Melampsora lini|flax rust]] (''Melampsora lini'').<ref Name="HH&GGE2004"/>
